q: Were the council to approve the plan, construction ___ next year.
explain: Were + subject + to-infinitive = formal hypothetical → would.

q: Little ___ that the castle had been watching them.
explain: Negative adverbial at the start → inversion: Little did they know.

q: Only after the gates had closed ___ their mistake.
explain: Only after… + inversion in the main clause.

q: It's essential that every member ___ present.
___ the heavy rain, the ceremony went ahead.
explain: Despite + noun; Although + clause; In spite OF.

q: The proposal, ___ merits are obvious, was rejected.
She'd sooner resign than ___ the truth.
explain: would sooner X than Y — both bare infinitives.

q: Not only ___ the treaty, but he also broke it.
Hardly had the debate started ___ the lights went out.
Should you need assistance, ___ hesitate to ask.
explain: Should you… = If you…; an imperative follows.

q: The minister is said ___ the decision before the vote.
explain: is said + perfect infinitive for an earlier action.

q: What I find most frustrating ___ the lack of transparency.
explain: A what-clause subject takes a singular verb.

q: Rarely ___ such eloquence in the council chamber.
It was the knight's courage, rather than his skill, ___ won the day.
explain: Cleft sentence: It was X that…

q: Had it not been for her intervention, the talks ___.
explain: Had it not been for = If it hadn't been for → would have + p.p.

q: So convincing ___ that the council changed its mind.
explain: So + adjective at the start → inversion with 'be'.
